title: Nested List Iterator
statement:
Implement a lazy iterator over a nested list of integers. Each element is a `NestedValue`, which holds either a single integer or a list of `NestedValue` elements (which may itself be empty or arbitrarily nested).

Implement `Solution(List<NestedValue> items)` with:
- `boolean hasNext()` — returns `true` if another integer remains in left-to-right flattened order.
- `int next()` — returns the next integer and advances the iterator. Throw `NoSuchElementException` if no integer remains.

Contract
- Do not flatten the entire input eagerly into a `List<Integer>` in the constructor unless you want to trade off lazy space; the intended design uses an explicit stack of iterators or elements so `hasNext()` and `next()` run in amortized `O(1)` time with `O(depth)` auxiliary stack space.
- Empty nested lists (such as `[[]]`, `[[], [1, []], []]`) must be skipped seamlessly so `hasNext()` returns `false` when only empty lists remain.
- Calling `hasNext()` multiple times in a row without calling `next()` must not skip elements.

Examples
- `[[1, 1], 2, [1, 1]]` -> `[1, 1, 2, 1, 1]`
- `[1, [4, [6]]]` -> `[1, 4, 6]`
- `[[], [[]], [3, []]]` -> `[3]`
hints: Maintain a stack (Deque) of Iterator<NestedValue> (or ListIterator / elements in reverse order) starting with items.iterator() on top.
Write a helper advance() called by hasNext() that keeps expanding the top iterator until either the stack is empty or the next integer is staged in a field (e.g., Integer nextValue).

When next() is called, ensure hasNext() is true (otherwise throw NoSuchElementException), capture nextValue, clear it to null, and return it. Intended complexity: O(n) total time across a full traversal (amortized O(1) per element), O(depth) space (O(n) worst case).
inputSyntax: Input: nested integer list, for example: [[1,1],2,[1,1]]
